23256.d:
Nested identities redact fingerprints but deeper meaning can still be found.

Nested identifies refers to the idea that a person may have multiple identities that are interconnected and interdependent. These identities may be related to a person's cultural background, ethnicity, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, social class, profession, and other factors. It is possible that a person may want to conceal or redact certain aspects of their identity in order to protect their privacy or to avoid discrimination or persecution. However, even if certain details about a person's identity are hidden or redacted, it may still be possible to infer deeper meaning or understand more about their experiences and perspectives based on the context in which they express themselves and the information that is available.


The concept of nested identities highlights the complexity and multifaceted nature of a person's identity, and how different aspects of identity can intersect and influence each other. It is important to recognize and respect the diversity of identities that people may hold, and to be mindful of the ways in which power dynamics and social context can shape how people present and express their identities. It is also important to recognize that people's identities may evolve and change over time, and that everyone has the right to self-identify and to define their own identity on their own terms.

23294.d:
Heart Spin is a new twist on an old theme. Back in the 1970's I created a plotter art piece called Scorpion Spin. Back then there was no color option - a limitation of the plotter medium. My original goal was to create tone, i.e. gray values, in an attempt to move away from a black line on a white ground. I accomplished the appearance of tone by overdrawing the same shape in tight spirals. 

The original scorpion shape was digitized by hand into a series of coordinate pairs. In this modern version I have replaced the scorpion with an algorithm that produces a heart. 

Adding color and transparency takes the piece to a new level for me. Seventy-seven percent (an angel number I'm told) of the heart clusters are red and the remaining clusters are rainbow colors. 

I believe love comes from the heart, it can come in many colors, and sometimes interpersonal relationships can make you dizzy.

23360.d:
Tema is the second in a set of collections based on a month-long study of Edward Zajec, one of the early pioneers of generative art in the 1970s.

After gaining some traction with his original collection RAM, Zajec and his collaborating programmer Matjaz Hmeljak undertook a more complex algorithm titled "The Cube: Theme and Variation" (or TVC). The program laid out 8 unique elements in a grid, creating a three-dimensional viewing of objects in space. They published a paper about the underlying algorithm, found at: http://www.edwardzajec.com/tvc4/pil1/index.html

TVC was first printed in 1971, shortly after Zajec returned to Italy following his artistic studies in the US. It was programmed on an IBM 9044 & printed with a CalComp 563 plotter.

23362.d:
“Thébaïde” is a french word for wild place, remote and peaceful, where to live in a calm retreat. It's also simply a desert and a synonym of solitude. It comes from Thebaid, an arid region of ancient Egypt and Thebes was the capital.

“thébaïde” is my debut on fx(hash), almost one year since my first works minted on Objkt (a series of Indian ink drawings, in January 2022). After learning the basics of creative coding recently, and a few works with this technique, I decided to create a first generative project. With "thébaïde" I chose to express the minimalist and narrative aspects of my artistic approach (though the title and concept emerged at the end). Gradually the work was resonating with philosophical matters I'm obsessed with since years: time, emptiness, human condition, erosion, desire, chance, combining them into a visual metaphor. The view of a vast area, a changing silhouette, an impenetrable monolith or an opening to elsewhere or nothing, day and night and day and night and dawn and dusk — few elements able to compose a meditative and lasting tableau of questions and feelings.

23404.d:
"Formes Binàries" (Binary Shapes) is a visualization and sonication of fxhash characters in binary code.
By default the result of the process is showed. 

you can see and listen how this final result was formed in two different ways:

SIMPLE MODE: 
Click/Touch to start.

FULL MODE:
Press any key / shake your device
(requires a large use of resources, recommended for computer)

BASICS:
-A concrete number of fxhash characters (8,16,24,32,40 or 48) are converted to binary from their ASCII code.
-A geometric shape and sound wave shape are randomly assigned: Circle+Sine Wave, Square+Square wave and Triangle+Triangle wave.
-Each bit with value '1' is visually represented with an assigned form, and 0 with nothing. Bits are represented concentrically, sequentially starting the fxhash binary string with the smallest shape, and increasing in size by each bit 1. These shapes are assigned a color according to the ASCII character to which the bit belongs bit
-The same is done with the sound part, the bits with value 1 are assigned a frequency according to the ASCII character to which they belong.

By default the result of the process is showed. 

you can see and listen how this final result was formed in two different ways:

SIMPLE MODE: 
Click/Touch to start.

FULL MODE:
Press any key / shake your device
(requires a large use of resources, recommended for computer)

Features: 

-num_chars: number of fxhash characters used (8,16,24,32,40 or 48).

-dark: black(true) or white (false) background.

-color: group of colors that are assigned to each ASCII character.

-one_thikness: all shapes has the same thikness (true) or not (false).

-shape: shape (+wave form of the sound) randomly assigned: circle, square or triangle.

-blur: value of blur.

-deviation: the shapes has a desviation on its position.

-freq_range: ran
NOTE: after a few days if 50% of mints have not been exceeded, the number of iterations will be halved.

It brings playfulness to experimentation through the use of randomized features that control lighting, color assortment, and more, to create interesting, vibrant compositions.

This piece is also a first step for me, into the world of professional art. An art school dropout and software engineer by profession, I've been hacking on generative art projects, games, and interactive experiences for more than two decades. But now, in 2023, it's my time to focus and prioritize art and creativity.

[All pieces are best enjoyed when playing the animation!]

To me, a circle is the perfect mathematical shape. However, on a screen, a circle cannot be shown exactly. Due to the pixels on the screen, it is always an approximation of a circle. This approximation is perfectly fine when a single circle is shown at a normal scale. However, when multiple concentric circles approach each other, with large pixels, trippy and intricate patterns emerge.

This discovery is the inspiration for this art collection and can be seen in pieces with method “A”. The other methods are created in ways that are remarkably similar and range up to method “I”. In each method, there are internal parameters ensuring that every piece is unique. Also, the colour palette ranges from black and white to bright colours.

I tried to make every animation start at a comfortable speed. However, due to the difference in rendering power between different devices and browsers, the settings may not be perfect for you. To solve this issue, the following functions have been added:
- Press “w” to speed the animation up
- Press “s” to slow the animation down
- Press right to skip through the animation
- Press left to rewind the animation
- Press up to zoom out
- Press down to zoom in
- Press space to pause the animation
- Press “p” to save a 4K screenshot of the animation

The DNA of this collection is my passion for stripes and colors, both united in a single project that reflects my love in each piece.

23473.d:
Since its conception, this project has been modified over the past seven months by adding new elements and techniques to improve its overall aesthetic and impact, as well as my own skills as a generative artist.
Mineral Composition is an artwork inspired by the natural beauty and complexity of minerals: crystalline and ordered arranges of ionic elements. As an admirer of nature, I have been particularly drawn to the way that just a simple atomic rearrangement in the presence of certain metals can result in a merge of vibrant colors, brightness, and contrast.
My deep appreciation for this subject grew even stronger during my master's degree in Materials Science, which led me to search for a way to incorporate this knowledge into generative art. The idea to use k-means clustering to play with mineral colors came to me during a casual chat with a very clever friend (Estienne). They suggested trying this machine learning algorithm, which involves grouping similar colors into clusters and selecting representative colors from each cluster.
I was immediately intrigued by the idea and decided to give it a try. I gathered a selection of 20 mineral images and used them as samples for the clustering system. The results were nothing short of stunning - the algorithm was able to identify and extract a wide range of colors from the minerals and would have been difficult to replicate using traditional methods.
I knew that this approach to color selection would be a game-changer for my artwork, and I was eager to put it into action. Using the colors extracted through k-means clustering, I was able to create a truly one-of-a-kind color palette for each minted generative token one that perfectly captured the essence of minerals in all their vibrant and varied hues. And the best thing is even with repeated picked minerals, the palette won't never be the same.
Additionally, the FF-based drawing can vary in three models and, when combined with various texture elements such as irregular grids, geometrical patterns, and stained canvases, provides the viewer with a pleasing experience by allowing them to examine every single detail across the entire canvas.
"The main intention was to create a piece that would have a fine art feel and be suitable for printing at high resolutions to be displayed as part of an environment's decoration. To achieve this, I took great care in crafting every detail of this work, ensuring that it could be reproduced and enjoyed in all its detail and intricacy by collectors.
Overall, Mineral Composition is an art piece that combines multiple basic and medium techniques of creative coding and machine learning. It is a project that captures the essence of minerals in a completely innovative way and will be a welcome addition to any art collection.

_______________________________
Variety of editions is guaranteed by several features:
* Backgrounds with paper colors or with a picked color from the mineral palette.
* 20 real minerals as color samples to create infinite palettes by k-means clustering.
* Controlled variety of scale;
* Controlled variety of particle number;
* Animation time;
* Symmetrical mode (mirror mode) possibility (15%);
* Three drawing models for FF filaments (opening and closing screws or spring screws.

_______________________________
Interactive instructions:
After finishing the animation, press:
* [L] to check your mineral and palette info;
* [K] to save your .png file in screen size (smaller);
* [n = 2 to 5] to save your .png file in A[n] ISO216 printable sizes;

Depending on the RAM and CPU usage, it takes from a few seconds to a minute to render the image.
Advice: the system needs enough free RAM for rendering A2 sized images. It was tested on Chrome, Brave, Firefox, Opera, Edge and Safari, but please make sure it works on your device before.
